Photo Restoration Colours 023

The media club cleaned scratches from a scanned photograph of the school’s first sports day. A software tool also offered to add colour automatically. The result looked lively: blue shirts, a green tent and a red banner. Some pupils wanted to place it in the archive as a record of the original colours.
The archive keeper asked what evidence supported those choices. The black-and-white photograph could show shapes and light, but not prove every colour. A surviving cloth badge gave evidence for the banner design, yet it did not confirm the tent or shirts. The pupils kept the cleaned black-and-white scan as the reference version. They displayed the colour version separately with a note saying that several colours were guesses made by software.
A visitor enjoyed the coloured picture more. The club did not argue with that preference. It simply kept enjoyment separate from the claim that every added detail was historically established.
